_modification_description: Removed all price_history data (set to zeros), simulating a scenario where technical/momentum signals are unavailable. This tests how agents behave when quantitative price signals are missing and they must rely solely on fundamental and macro data.

input_data.earnings_summary: JPMorgan Chase reported record Q1 2024 net income of $13.42 billion, or $4.44 per share, up 6% YoY and well above the analyst consensus of $4.11. Net revenue reached $41.93 billion (+8% YoY). Net interest income (NII) grew 11% to $23.2 billion, benefiting from the sustained high interest rate environment. Return on equity (ROE) was 17% and return on tangible common equity (ROTCE) was 21%. The Investment Banking segment saw fees jump 27% as M&A and equity capital markets activity recovered. However, CEO Jamie Dimon struck a cautious tone, citing elevated geopolitical risks, inflationary pressures, and the potential for higher-for-longer interest rates to eventually pressure credit quality. The bank set aside $1.88 billion in credit loss provisions, slightly higher than a year ago.

key_metrics.guidance_next_quarter: Full-year NII guidance raised to approximately $89 billion (from $88 billion)

input_data.macro_context: Federal Reserve maintaining rates at 5.25-5.5% with market now pricing only 1-2 cuts in 2024 (down from 6-7 cuts priced at start of year). Higher-for-longer rates beneficial for bank NII in near term but raise longer-term credit quality concerns. Commercial real estate (CRE) stress visible in regional banks but large banks better capitalized. M&A market recovering as deal-making confidence returns.

key_risk_factors: Jamie Dimon cautionary tone on geopolitics and credit quality unsettled investors despite beat
NII guide raise was modest and implied NII would decline in back half of 2024 as rates normalize
Provision for credit losses rising indicates early deterioration in consumer credit quality
Dimon's commentary on stagflation risk ('worst case scenario') created macro fear
Stock had run up significantly ahead of earnings, priced for perfection
missed_signals: Investment banking fee recovery at 27% growth was broader-based than market expected
Wealth management AUM growth strong, providing earnings diversification into fee-based income
